# Engine: `blockAt`, reviewer-prefixed finding ids, per-reviewer provider/model, and comment routing

## What to build

Already in the codebase (earlier slices): `packages/graph-execution/src/review/reviewers.ts` (`type Reviewer` with `id`, `type: "diff"|"tester"`, `name`, `instructions`, `repoFile`, `provider?` (one of `REVIEWER_PROVIDERS = ["claude","codex","opencode","qwen","fake"]`), `model?`, `files?`, `blockAt: "major"|"blocker"|"never"` (default `major`), `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS`, `stepName`, `notPerformed`, `reviewerAgent`, `readRunReviewers(runDir)`); `runReviewPhase({ ..., reviewers })` runs every enabled reviewer of the run in `reviewRound` (diff reviewers via `runCodeReviewer({ ...shared, kind, name, reviewer })`, the tester via `runLiveTester`), each with its own instructions and repo file; `preflight` returns `reviewers` (enabled) and `reviewersFile`; `execute()` in `runner/run.ts` reads `reviewers = await readRunReviewers(ctx.runDir)`.

This slice adds the remaining per-reviewer behaviour of the spec (`docs/prd/ui-reviewers.md`, "Engine: review round", decisions on `blockAt`, finding ids, providers, comments; KAN-87):
1. **`blockAt`**: `major` (default; blockers and majors start a fix pass, as today), `blocker` (only blockers start one), `never` (every finding of that reviewer is reported as **minor** when the report is read, so it shows in the summary as minor and never starts a fix pass).
2. **Finding id prefix**: findings of reviewers other than `code` and `tester` get `<id>-` prepended when the report is normalized, unless already prefixed (`F1` → `security-F1`). Two reviewers can no longer both report `F1`. `plan-*` and `human-*` ids are never prefixed.
3. **Per-reviewer provider and model**: a reviewer runs with its own `provider`/`model`, falling back to the run's `--provider`/`--model`. `getProvider` is called for every distinct provider at startup, so a missing CLI (e.g. `codex` not on `PATH`) fails with exit 2 before the run is created, and the same on `--resume`.
4. **Human comments** and their verdicts go to the `code` reviewer if it is enabled, else to the first enabled `diff` reviewer; exactly one reviewer answers each comment. With no diff reviewer, comments get no verdict (`applyCommentVerdicts` marks them `not_fixed`, as today when the reviewer gives none).
5. README: document the reviewers file.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/report.ts`:
  - lines 44-57 `reportSchema`; 163-170 `normalizeReport` (downgrades blocker/major without `failureScenario` to minor); 228-233 `openBlocking(report)` — used by `review/phase.ts` (lines ~152, ~177, ~191, ~252) and `agents/fixer.ts` (`fixerPrompt`); 327-338 `readReport`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts` `reviewRound` (`runOne(reviewer)`: `readReport(file, round, kind)` reuse, `runner(...)`, `applyTestPlan`, `applyCommentVerdicts` for `kind === "code" && humanRound > 0`, the `RetriesExhaustedError` branch carrying `previous(kind)` unresolved findings, `comments` passed only for `kind === "code"`), `ReviewPhaseOptions` (`provider`, `model`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/human.ts` lines 142-154 `applyCommentVerdicts` ("Code reviewer: …" evidence text), 178-200 `commentOutcomes` — reads verdicts from `code.json` only (line 181); used by `web/server.ts:223` and `suite/server.ts:163`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/agents/reviewer.ts` `runReviewAgent` (`opts.comments?.length` check), `CodeReviewerOptions.comments`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/providers/index.ts` lines 56-80 `getProvider(name, cwd)` (throws `the "<bin>" CLI was not found on the PATH; …`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/launch/preflight.ts` `checkEnvironment` (line 68-85, `getProvider` at 83), `preflight` (returns `{ kind: "run", tasks, layers, env, reviewers, reviewersFile }`), `preflightResume` (line 216 `getProvider(state.provider, repo)`; returns `provider`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/run.ts` lines 255-275 (the run provider wrapped as `teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(trackProcesses(ctx.provider, ctx.runDir), …), …), events)`), the `runReviewPhase({...})` call (~line 491).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/startup.ts` `RunContext` (has `provider: Provider`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` lines 315-330 ("exits 2 at startup when --provider codex is not on the PATH": how PATH is limited for a spawned CLI).
- `packages/graph-execution/README.md` lines 269-275 (`## REVIEW.md and TESTING.md (optional)`), line 84 (usage line), lines 95-110 (options table), lines 359-366 (`## The review loop`).

## Patterns to follow

**Report post-processing in the phase, written back to the report file** (phase.ts `runOne`):
```ts
let report = kind === "tester" && context.testPlan ? applyTestPlan(raw, context.testPlan, previous(kind)) : raw;
if (kind === "code" && humanRound > 0) report = applyCommentVerdicts(raw, comments);
if (report !== raw) await writeFile(file, `${JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)}\n`);
```

**Provider wrapping** in `execute()` must be applied to every provider used by an agent (loop/idle watchdogs, process tracking, output tee to `logs/<label>.log`).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/report.ts`

- `reportSchema`: add `/** Set by the tool from the reviewer's \`blockAt\` when it is \`blocker\`: only blockers keep the loop going. */ blockAt: z.enum(["blocker"]).optional()`.
- `openBlocking`: `report.findings.filter((f) => f.status !== "fixed" && (report.blockAt === "blocker" ? f.severity === "blocker" : f.severity !== "minor"))`.
- New `export function applyReviewerRules(report: Report, r: { id: string; blockAt: "major" | "blocker" | "never" }): Report`:
  - ids: for `r.id` not `code`/`tester`, every finding whose id does not start with `${r.id}-`, `plan-` or `human-` becomes `${r.id}-${id}`;
  - `never`: every finding gets `severity: "minor"`;
  - `blocker`: sets `blockAt: "blocker"`; `major`/`never`: no `blockAt` key (so built-in report files stay byte-identical);
  - returns the same object when nothing changed (identity check is used to decide whether to rewrite the file).
- **GOTCHA**: re-reviews keep the ids of the previous report (already prefixed), so the prefixing must be idempotent.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts`

- `ReviewPhaseOptions`: add `/** Providers by name for reviewers with their own \`provider\`; the run's \`provider\` otherwise. */ providers?: Readonly<Record<string, Provider>>;`
- In `runOne(reviewer)`:
  - `const provider = reviewer.provider ? (opts.providers?.[reviewer.provider] ?? (reviewer.provider === opts.provider.name ? opts.provider : undefined)) : opts.provider;` — throw `new Error(\`no provider ${reviewer.provider} for reviewer ${reviewer.id}\`)` when undefined (cannot happen after the startup check). `model: reviewer.model ?? opts.model`. Put both into the runner options instead of `shared.provider`/`shared.model`.
  - After the runner (and after `applyTestPlan` / comment verdicts) and also on the reused-report and gave-up paths: `report = applyReviewerRules(report, reviewer)`; rewrite the file when it changed. The reused report (`readReport` of an existing file) is already processed, applying again is a no-op.
  - Comment routing: compute once per round `const commentsBy = reviewers.find((r) => r.id === "code")?.id ?? reviewers.find((r) => r.type === "diff")?.id;` Pass `comments` and run `applyCommentVerdicts` only for `kind === commentsBy` (replaces the three `kind === "code"` comment checks, including the `RetriesExhaustedError` branch).
- **GOTCHA**: `applyReviewerRules` comes after `applyCommentVerdicts`, so `human-*` findings stay unprefixed; `normalizeReport` (failureScenario rule) still runs first inside `runReviewAgent`/`readReport`.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/human.ts`

- `commentOutcomes`: read the verdicts from whichever report in `reports/round<round>/` has a `comments` array: list `*.json` files in the dir except `fixer-comments.json`, read each with `readReport(file, round, <basename without .json>)`, take the first with `comments`. Keep reading `tester.json` for `liveCheck` cases. Missing dir → `{}` as today.
- `applyCommentVerdicts` text `no verdict from the code reviewer` / `Code reviewer: ` stays (it is shown in the UI; wording change not needed).

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/launch/preflight.ts`

- New exported helper: `export async function checkReviewerProviders(reviewers: readonly Reviewer[], runProvider: string, repo: string): Promise<void>` — for every distinct `r.provider` that differs from `runProvider`, `await getProvider(name, repo)`, wrapping an error as `UsageError(\`reviewer "${r.id}": ${err.message}\`)`.
- `preflight` (run): after `checkEnvironment`, `await checkReviewerProviders(reviewers, opts.provider, env.repo)`.
- `preflightResume`: after `getProvider(state.provider, repo)`, `await checkReviewerProviders(await readRunReviewers(runDir), state.provider, repo)`.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/run.ts` (`execute`)

- After `const reviewers = await readRunReviewers(ctx.runDir);` build the providers map, wrapped like the run provider (extract the existing wrapping into a local `const wrap = (p: Provider): Provider => teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(trackProcesses(p, ctx.runDir), …), …), events);` and use it for `provider` too, keeping its behaviour):
  ```ts
  const providers: Record<string, Provider> = {};
  for (const name of new Set(reviewers.map((r) => r.provider).filter((p): p is string => p !== undefined && p !== ctx.provider.name))) {
    providers[name] = wrap(await getProvider(name, ctx.repo));
  }
  ```
  and pass `providers` to `runReviewPhase`.
- **IMPORTS**: `getProvider` from `../providers/index.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: other features of this suite also edit `run.ts`; keep the change to these lines.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/README.md`

- Usage line (84): add `[--reviewers <file>]`. Options table: a row for `--reviewers <file>`: "Reviewers file (JSON). Default: `$GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS`, else the built-in code reviewer and live tester. Copied into the run dir at start; not allowed with `--resume`. See [Reviewers file](#reviewers-file-optional)."
- New section `## Reviewers file (optional)` after `## REVIEW.md and TESTING.md (optional)`: the JSON example from the spec (code, tester, security), the field rules (id kebab-case 1-32 and unique, at most one `tester` with id `tester`, `repoFile` a `.md` name at the repo root and unique, `provider`/`model` fall back to the run's, `files` globs with `!` excludes, `blockAt` major/blocker/never), the two layers (general `instructions` + the reviewer's own repo file, only its own, a missing file is fine), finding id prefixes (`security-F1`), comment routing, that disabled reviewers are skipped and no enabled reviewer means the result is not reviewed, that suites keep the built-ins, and that graph-manager sets `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` for its runs. Add the section to the README's Contents list if it lists sections there (lines 37-42).

### Tests

- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/report.test.ts`: `applyReviewerRules` — prefix for `security`, idempotent, `plan-P1`/`human-c1` untouched, `code`/`tester` untouched; `never` → all minor; `blocker` → `openBlocking` returns only blockers; `major` → no `blockAt` key and identity returned.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase-reviewers.test.ts` (exists; add), with `runReview(script, { reviewers })` and the diamond fixture:
  - security reports `F1` major (with `failureScenario`) in round 0 and nothing in round 1 → `reports/round0/security.json` has id `security-F1`; the fixer prompt (`provider.calls` with `role === "fixer"`) contains `**security-F1** (major, Security)`; round 1's security prompt lists `security-F1` in its previous report.
  - same script with `blockAt: "never"` → no fixer call, exit 0, the finding is `minor` in `security.json`.
  - `blockAt: "blocker"` with a major → no fixer call; with a blocker → one fixer pass.
  - code reviewer and a `security` reviewer with `provider: "fake", model: "m2"` while the run uses the injected fake → the security call has `model: "m2"`, the code call the run's model.
- Comment routing (pattern: `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase-human.test.ts`): with `code` disabled and `security` + `tester` enabled, the open human comments appear in the `security-r1` prompt and its report's `comments` give the verdicts (`human-*` findings in `security.json`, unprefixed); with `code` enabled they go to `code` only.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts` (spawned CLI, pattern at lines 315-330): a reviewers file with `{ id: "security", type: "diff", name: "Security", repoFile: "SECURITY_REVIEW.md", provider: "codex" }` and `--provider fake`, with a PATH that holds `node` but no `codex` → exit 2, stderr contains `reviewer "security"` and `codex`, and no run dir exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `blockAt: "never"` with a major finding: no fix pass; the summary/report lists it as minor.
- [ ] `blockAt: "blocker"`: majors never start a fix pass, blockers do.
- [ ] Security findings reach the fixer as `security-F1`, …; `code`/`tester` ids unchanged.
- [ ] A reviewer with `provider: "codex"` while `codex` is not on `PATH` → exit 2 at startup (and on `--resume`).
- [ ] Each reviewer runs with its own provider/model, else the run's.
- [ ] Human comments are answered by `code` if enabled, else by the first enabled diff reviewer; the web view's comment outcomes still show the verdicts.
- [ ] Built-in default runs are unchanged; all existing tests pass.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- report phase human preflight cli
npm test
```
